topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series and sets out what students should learn from this lecture.

topics.label: Cellular changes and tissue organisation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics develop an account of cancer as altered cellular behaviour whose significance must be understood within organised tissues.

topics.label: Invasion and metastasis as features of malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how tumour spread distinguishes malignancy from benign growth and how that distinction appears clinically and histologically.

topics.label: Benign tumour progression and patient risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine what a benign tumour diagnosis implies for subsequent tumour behaviour and risk to the patient.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour names indicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming conventions.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour growth disrupts normal bodily function and produces potentially fatal disease.

topics.label: Tumour incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the occurrence of tumour types across populations and species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the rationale for detecting cancer early and assess how effectively screening achieves that goal in different tumour types.

topics.label: Lecture close and revision guidance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by returning to the learning outcomes and directing students towards revision and upcoming practicals.
